standard_prerequisites.name: Cone of a morphism of complexes and the characterisation of quasi-isomorphisms by acyclic cones
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the cone construction and the criterion that a morphism is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when its cone is acyclic
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the reduction of the statement to the acyclicity of a tensor product, which K-flatness provides.

core_obligations: Reduce to cones (proof lines 3248-3260): the author replaces the quasi-isomorphism by the acyclicity of its cone and observes that the induced map of total tensor products has cone the total tensor product of the given complex with the cone of the map.
Use K-flatness (proof lines 3260-3268): since the cone is acyclic and the complexes are K-flat, its total tensor product with the given complex is acyclic, so the induced map is a quasi-isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Replace the quasi-isomorphism by its acyclic cone.
Identify the cone of the induced map with the total tensor product with that cone.
Use K-flatness to conclude acyclicity and hence the quasi-isomorphism statement.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that tensoring a quasi-isomorphism of K-flat complexes with an arbitrary complex gives a quasi-isomorphism of total complexes (statement lines 3232-3246). The proof replaces the quasi-isomorphism by the acyclicity of its cone and identifies the cone of the induced map with the total tensor product of the given complex with that cone (proof lines 3248-3260), after which K-flatness gives the acyclicity and hence the conclusion (proof lines 3260-3268). The non-formal content is the identification of the cones. The claim is H2: one reduction plus one application of K-flatness.
